name: Melrose Abbey
summary: Melrose Abbey was a major Cistercian monastery in the Scottish Borders, later associated with the burial tradition of Robert the Bruce’s heart.
overview: Melrose Abbey was a Cistercian monastery in the Scottish Borders, founded under David I and deeply connected to monastic reform, border society, and royal patronage.
Later tradition links the abbey to the burial of Robert the Bruce’s heart after Sir James Douglas’s failed journey toward crusade.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Melrose Abbey mattered as a Cistercian house in a border region repeatedly affected by Anglo-Scottish war. Its religious life and landed wealth placed it inside both spiritual and political history.

contentSections.title: Medieval history
paragraphs: The abbey was founded in the twelfth century and became one of the great monastic institutions of medieval Scotland. Border warfare damaged such houses, but also made them important custodians of memory and documents.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: The Bruce heart tradition gave Melrose a lasting place in Scottish royal memory. Whether treated devotionally or historically, the tradition connects death, crusading ideals, and national commemoration.
